merger_name: Woolworths - supermarket e-commerce hub in Muswellbrook, NSW
merger_description:
Woolworths Group Limited (**Woolworths**) proposes to acquire a leasehold interest in respect of a parcel of land located at 76 Brook St, Muswellbrook, NSW (the **Target Site**) from Muswellbrook Shire Council.

Woolworths is an ASX-listed retailer operating a national supermarket network across Australia and New Zealand, which includes full-line stores, Woolworths Metro outlets, and customer fulfilment centres. Its broader operations encompass discount department stores, specialty retail, wholesale food supply, and data analytics.

Woolworths has an operational supermarket in Muswellbrook (**Woolworths Muswellbrook**), which is located adjacent to the Target Site.

Muswellbrook Shire Council is the local government authority overseeing the Muswellbrook Shire area in the Upper Hunter region of NSW, 127km north-west of Newcastle. Muswellbrook Shire Council owns a number of freehold sites in Muswellbrook, including the Woolworths Muswellbrook site and the Target Site.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the Target Site is unlikely to be able to accommodate a new
supermarket
b. the expansion of Woolworths’ existing supermarket site in
Muswellbrook is for the purposes of improving the quality of
the offering of Woolworths’ existing supermarket and its
e-commerce capabilities
c. there are alternative grocery retailers, including Coles and
ALDI, in the local area surrounding the Target Site.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds determined under section 51ABP(1) being met. The ACCC
does however observe that the targeted notification requirements for
supermarkets determined under section 51ABQ(1) are likely to apply.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
